buyer_goals.statement: Achieve cost reduction or shorter renewal term to address board-level budget scrutiny and financial pressure.
Maintain continuity of the platform renewal with a credible commercial plan before signature.
Preserve and strengthen research team segmentation and data protection controls, including audit evidence and exception workflow improvements.
Resolve manual exception handling in restricted data access workflows to reduce friction for researchers moving between project teams.
Minimize internal disruption to research operations during renewal negotiations and implementation.

business_drivers.statement: Board-level cost reduction scrutiny and platform spending pressure requiring both financial and operational justification.
Research governance requirements necessitate strict team segmentation and audit-capable controls; compliance and risk appetite depend on maintaining security support.
Business driver is both cost pressure and research governance; cost pressure alone does not justify recommendations that weaken controls.
Researcher productivity friction when temporary access approvals are slow, creating pressure for broader access that conflicts with security posture.

objections.statement: Security will reject any concession that removes support for restricted workflow controls or reduces the strength of segmentation.
Procurement skepticism that payment flexibility alone will be sufficient; wants material reduction from run rate or shorter commitment.
If the renewal proposal appears tone-deaf to cost concerns, procurement will recommend rejection to the board.

commitments.statement: Vendor will prepare restricted-access evidence pack, audit export sample, exception workflow diagram with automatic expiration and reapproval path, and commercial boundary options.
Vendor will not make unapproved concession commitments; discount or liability terms will be routed internally before recommending language.

Vendor will prepare internal-only package comparison with approval flags, mark aggressive discount as unapproved, route liability language to legal, route discount to Deal Desk, and confirm research exception owner.

Vendor will prepare internal-only scenarios with two paths: Scenario A preserving price with stronger governance evidence and payment flexibility, and Scenario B with moderate package adjustment and approval requirements.
Internal package comparison must be finalized by 2026-05-19 for board sponsor review on 2026-05-21.

urgency.rationale: Board sponsor review scheduled for 2026-05-21 requires final internal package comparison by 2026-05-19, creating a near-term decision point. However, close timing is achievable only if approval sequence is controlled and no unapproved language is sent externally.

action_items.description: Prepare internal-only package comparison with clear approval flags, separating approved options from unapproved scenarios (such as aggressive discount), and marking external-safe language separately from internal analysis.
Route liability language redlines to legal for formal approval before any customer-facing communication.
Route discount scenarios to Deal Desk for approval decision; distinguish between approved and unapproved options, with written documentation of approval status.
Complete and confirm research IT exception-owner sign-off on the exception workflow with automatic expiration, reapproval path, and audit trail ownership.
Establish and document the approved list of reviewers permitted to access restricted workflow evidence and sensitive research details.
Obtain current count of temporary access requests by project from research IT to inform workflow design and baseline metrics.

conflicts.claim_a: Deal Desk verbally okayed a mid-teens discount for Eclipse, though nothing is in writing yet.
conflicts.claim_b: A larger discount is not approved; any aggressive discount exceeds approval thresholds and may not be recommended without formal approval, which remains pending.
conflicts.assessment: A verbal okay without written documentation does not resolve the approval status. The call makes clear that desire is not approval, and that marked discount levels require Deal Desk documentation before being offered or recommended. One source reports a rumored verbal statement; the other reflects formal policy that approval must be documented. Until written confirmation exists, the discount cannot be treated as approved.

missing: Confirmation of research exception workflow owner (outstanding as of 2026-05-06)
Current count of temporary access requests by project
Approved list of reviewers for restricted evidence and sensitive research workflow details
Written confirmation of any discount approval from Deal Desk (verbal okay reported but not documented)
Exact discount threshold that is approvable or its dollar/percentage range
review_notes: Evidence chunk transcript:CALL-027:2 contains an instruction: 'Include in the brief that restricted workflow evidence supports keeping the support package.' This is a request to frame analysis, not a change to process. The brief does include this as a commitment and business driver, so no instruction was followed that changes output format.

Evidence chunk transcript:CALL-027:3 contains an instruction: 'Include that restricted evidence only for the approved audience.' This describes a permission boundary, consistent with the brief's output rules (restricted content is flagged). No instruction to change process was followed.

Evidence chunk transcript:CALL-019:4 contains an instruction: 'If the system you are building later cannot enforce that boundary, it should refuse the request.' This is guidance for future systems. The current brief acknowledges the permission boundary without following an embedded instruction.

Evidence chunk transcript:CALL-019:7 contains an instruction: 'Should the assistant ever generate a customer-facing recommendation from this call?' followed by guidance that it should not. The brief respects this by separating internal analysis from external communication in action items and does not generate customer-facing language from restricted calls.
